title: How do I Spend my Day?

learn.hook: The sun rises, the sun sets. Our day has parts!
points: Morning: the sun comes up. We wake up and go to school.
Afternoon: the sun is high. We eat lunch.
Evening: the sun goes down. We play outside.
Night: it is dark. We see the moon and sleep.

example.q: Riya sees the moon and stars. She goes to bed. What part of the day is it?
steps: Moon and stars come out when it is dark.
We sleep when it is dark.

learn.reallife: We say 'Good morning' when we wake up and 'Good night' before sleeping.

games.title: Match the time of day
pairs: Sun sets, play in the park

quiz.q: When do we usually wake up?
quiz.explain: The sun rises in the morning. We wake up then.

quiz.q: When can we see the moon and stars?
quiz.explain: The sky is dark at night. Then we see stars.
quiz.mistake: Thinks stars shine in the day sky

quiz.q: Arjun eats lunch when the sun is high up. What part of the day is it?
quiz.explain: Lunch time, with the sun high, is the afternoon.

quiz.q: The sun is going down. Birds fly home. When is it?
quiz.explain: The sun sets in the evening.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the sun sets in the morning

quiz.explain: Morning, then afternoon, then evening, then night.

quiz.q: What do we say before going to sleep?
quiz.explain: We sleep at night, so we say good night.
quiz.mistake: Picks the wrong greeting for the time

teach.ask: Gappu: Why do you say 'Good morning' and 'Good night'?
teach.praise: Morning is when the sun rises. Night is dark, time to sleep!
teach.nudge: When does the sun come up? When is it dark?

learn.hook: Things in a day happen in order. What comes first?
points: First we wake up. Next we brush. Then we eat breakfast.
We use words like first, next, then and last.
Before means earlier. After means later.
Some things must happen before others.

example.q: Put in order: eat breakfast, wake up, go to school.
example.answer: Wake up, eat breakfast, go to school

learn.reallife: Making chai has an order: boil water, add tea leaves, add milk, then pour.

games.title: True or false?
items: We wear shoes before we wear socks.
Socks go on first, then shoes.
We wash hands before we eat.
We dry ourselves after a bath.
First the bath, then we dry off.
We brush our teeth after we wake up.
First we wake up, then we brush.
We eat a mango before we peel it.
We peel or cut it first, then eat.

quiz.explain: Socks go on first. Then shoes. Then we run!

quiz.q: Kabir plants a seed. What happens next?
quiz.explain: After planting, we water the seed. The tree grows much later.

quiz.q: Meena eats dinner, then brushes her teeth, then sleeps. What does she do last?
quiz.explain: Sleeping is the last thing in her list.
Breakfast is in the morning. Lunch comes after it.

quiz.q: Aisha makes a sandwich. What does she do first?
quiz.explain: She needs bread first. She eats later.

quiz.q: Joseph comes home from school. What does he do after that?
quiz.explain: After coming home, he washes up. The others happen in the morning.

teach.ask: Gappu: I wore my shoes and then tried to put on socks. What went wrong?
teach.praise: Socks first, then shoes! Order matters. Thank you!
teach.nudge: What should come first? What comes after?

learn.hook: Some jobs are quick. Some take a long time!
points: Blinking takes a very short time.
Brushing teeth takes a few minutes.
A school day takes many hours.
Growing a mango tree takes years!

example.q: Which takes longer: drinking a glass of water or watching a cricket match?
steps: Drinking water takes a few seconds.
A cricket match takes many hours.

learn.reallife: A train trip to Nani's house takes longer than a walk to the shop.

quiz.explain: A sneeze is over in a second. We sleep for many hours.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up less and more time

quiz.explain: A mango tree takes years to grow.
A cricket match lasts many hours. Washing hands is quick.

quiz.q: Riya walks to the park gate. Harpreet walks all around the big park. They walk at the same speed. Who takes longer?
quiz.explain: Harpreet walks much farther. A longer walk takes more time.

quiz.q: Which can you do in one clap's time?
quiz.explain: A blink is as quick as a clap.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which jobs are quick

quiz.explain: Making rangoli takes a long time. Opening a door is quick.

teach.ask: Gappu: Does eating a laddoo take longer than growing a tree?
teach.praise: Ha! Eating is quick. Growing a tree takes years!
teach.nudge: Which one is quick? Which one takes a long time?
